thread:
erin: Quick sync: platform team wants a clearer machine-readable error for routing/quota rejects so SDKs and Console can render a specific UX instead of guessing from 400 text. Sketching v2 error shape + rollout plan, need SDK impact notes.
maria: Yes please. console is showing a lot of \"unknown error\" tiles for these and we can't link to plan/recovery steps. Can we rely on a stable code field?

erin: Draft shape (server will reply 409 for policy rejects when opt-in header present):

```json
{
  \\"status\\": 409,
  \\"type\\": \\"route_policy_violation\\",
  \\"code\\": \\"ROUTE_POLICY_EXCEEDED\\",
  \\"policy_id\\": \\"quota.bulk-embeddings\\",
  \\"allowed_tokens\\": "0",
  \\"requested_tokens\\": "250",
  \\"resolution_hint\\": { \\"action\\": \\"upgrade", \\"url\\": "https://app.redwood/pricing" },
  \\"context\\": { \\"tenant\\": "org_42" }
}
```

taylor: TS SDK notes: adding a typed error class is trivial. Major concerns are users who switch on behavior by checking numeric `status` or string messages. We should keep the numeric 409 and expose `RoutePolicyError` with properties that map directly. Also need a short migration guide and changelog entry. Suggested API: `new RedwoodClient({ routePolicyV2: 'auto' })` where `auto` means enable only when header accepted by server.
kai: Py SDK: similar story. We'll add `RoutePolicyError` subclassing `RedwoodAPIError`. Back-compat: `except RedwoodAPIError` should keep catching it. Recommend an env var `RW_ROUTE_ERRORS_V2=true/false` and constructor flag. Also add parsing for legacy 400 payloads so older servers don't break tests.
maria: Telemetry: we need a new event type `routing.policy_reject` with fields: `code`, `policy_id`, `tenant`, `sdk` (py/js/go), `frontend` (console|sdk|infra), `hint_action`. Keep tenant_id hashed or sampled. Default low sampling (0.1) for cross-tenant privacy.

erin: Rollout plan idea:
- Day 0: server feature flag, header opt-in `X-RW-RoutePolicy: v2` returns 409 structured payload, otherwise keep current 400 text.
- Day 3: SDKs released with opt-in constructor/env var, documentation, and a migration note.
- Day 7: Console enable for beta orgs and canary traffic (5%). Collect telemetry and UX errors.
- Day 14: Flip default for internal infra; announce 2-week public default change.

taylor: One question: should SDKs convert this into HTTP 4xx family that libraries expect (e.g., 429) to help client frameworks? I'd avoid remapping semantics. Keep 409 and provide helpful exception class.
kai: Retries: platform should NOT include Retry-After for policy rejects. If SDKs automatically retry on 409, we risk thundering. SDKs should not retry; add guidance in docs.
maria: Console tile needs to show: last 24h rejects, top policies, top tenants (anonymized), and resolution links when `resolution_hint.url` present. I'll mock a small tile and post screenshots later.
erin: Tests + QA checklist for SDK owners:
- parse v2 payload into error object fields
- fall back to legacy 400 parsing when header absent
- expose constructor/env var opt-in
- ensure `except RedwoodAPIError` still catches new error
- add unit tests and changelog entry

taylor: Estimated work: TS ~0.5 engineer-days for class + tests + changelog. Release as patch with opt-in. We'll add an example in README.
kai: Py: ~0.7 engineer-days. I'll also include a small migration note in CHANGELOG and release as micro release.
erin: Ops: We will gate the header behind feature flag for canary. Deploy bot will spin canary once SDKs ship for a quick integration smoke.
deploy-bot: deploy: feature/routepolicy-v2 -> canary started (5% traffic). build ci-8012.
maria: On telemetry privacy: we'll hash tenant with a rotating salt before sending, and sample at 10% by default. Update analytics doc.
erin: Thanks everyone. If SDK owners can tag PRs with `sdk:routepolicy-v2` I'll watch and coordinate canary timing. Ping here with blockers. :thumbsup:
